items.title: Bengal Tiger
items.subtitle: Panthera tigris tigris
items.oneline: India’s national animal. A big striped cat of forests, grasslands and the Sundarbans mangroves.
idmarks: Orange coat with black vertical stripes; each tiger’s pattern is unique
White spots on the back of the ears
facts: India has about 3,682 tigers, as per the All India Tiger Estimation 2022
Project Tiger, India’s tiger-saving programme, began in 1973
Madhya Pradesh has the most tigers among states
traps: Tiger is Endangered, not Critically Endangered
Sundarbans is a Ramsar site, a UNESCO site and a biosphere reserve, all at once

places.name: Jim Corbett NP
places.note: India’s first national park (1936); Project Tiger launched here

places.name: Sundarbans TR
places.note: Only mangrove tiger habitat; shared with Bangladesh

places.name: Kanha TR
places.note: Sal and grassland; also home of hard-ground barasingha

places.name: Ranthambore TR
places.note: Dry deciduous forest in the Aravalli–Vindhya junction

newsTriggers.what: A tigress from Bihar was released into Buxa Tiger Reserve to open Wildlife Week 2026 and start a phased tiger recovery programme there.
newsTriggers.why: Buxa had no confirmed tiger sightings for decades; it shows how ‘empty’ reserves are being restocked.

newsTriggers.what: A government review flagged 25 of the 58 tiger reserves for priority action because tigers there are few or absent.
newsTriggers.why: Having more reserves does not mean every reserve has tigers.

newsTriggers.what: A tiger was found dead in Panna Tiger Reserve, the 28th tiger death in Madhya Pradesh since January 2026.
newsTriggers.why: High tiger numbers in MP also mean more deaths and conflict.

newsTriggers.what: A tiger and a cub died in Kanha Tiger Reserve, taking Madhya Pradesh’s tiger deaths for the year to 27.
newsTriggers.why: Repeated deaths in MP reserves keep the state in the news.

newsTriggers.what: A ‘Lion’ spotlight event at Sasan Gir was held ahead of India’s first International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Summit in New Delhi.
newsTriggers.why: IBCA is India’s alliance for seven big cats; tiger, lion and snow leopard are among them.

newsTriggers.what: The sixth All India Tiger Estimation is under way across the country. The final report is expected in 2027.
newsTriggers.why: Until the report is out, 3,682 tigers (2022) stays the official figure.

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2014 & 2017: M-STrIPES digital monitoring tool context for tiger reserves.
UPSC CSE Prelims 2020: Critical Tiger Habitats (CTH) declaration authority & largest CTH (Nagarjunsagar–Srisailam).

items.title: Asiatic Lion
items.subtitle: Panthera leo persica
items.oneline: Lives in the wild only in Gujarat’s Gir landscape, and nowhere else in the world.
idmarks: Shorter, sparser mane than African lions, so the ears stay visible
Longitudinal fold of skin along the belly
facts: 2025 population estimation: 891 lions in the Saurashtra landscape
Lions now also live outside protected areas in Amreli and Bhavnagar
traps: Kuno NP (MP) was prepared for lions but received African cheetahs in 2022

statusBadges.iucnNote: Sources differ here. Older assessments list it as Endangered, while lions as a species are Vulnerable and the Asiatic lion is now often grouped under Panthera leo leo. Check the IUCN site before teaching.

places.name: Gir NP & WLS
places.note: The only wild population of the Asiatic lion

places.name: Barda WLS
places.note: Being developed as a second home for lions

newsTriggers.what: On World Lion Day (10 August), the government highlighted growth from 523 lions in 2015 to 891 in 2025.
newsTriggers.why: Remember 891 (2025 count) and that all of them live in Gujarat.

newsTriggers.what: About 11 lions, mostly cubs, died in the Gir region in May 2026. Early signs pointed to babesiosis, a tick-borne infection.
newsTriggers.why: Shows the risk of keeping a species’ only wild population in one place.

newsTriggers.what: A ‘Lion’ spotlight event at Sasan Gir was held ahead of India’s first International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Summit in New Delhi.
newsTriggers.why: IBCA is India’s alliance for seven big cats; tiger, lion and snow leopard are among them.

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2019: Asiatic lion is naturally found in India only (Gir landscape).
UPSC CSE Prelims 2014 & 2017: Kuno-Palpur proposed translocation site for Asiatic Lion from Gir.

items.title: Greater One-horned Rhinoceros
items.subtitle: Rhinoceros unicornis
items.oneline: A large one-horned grazer of the tall, wet grasslands of Assam, North Bengal and the Terai.
idmarks: A single horn on the snout
Thick skin in armour-like folds, studded with wart-like bumps
facts: Was listed Endangered until 2008; recovery moved it to Vulnerable
Horn is compacted keratin, not bone
traps: Pobitora has the highest density, Kaziranga the largest number

places.name: Kaziranga NP
places.note: UNESCO site (1985); about two-thirds of the world’s population

places.name: Pobitora WLS
places.note: Highest rhino density in the world

places.name: Orang NP
places.note: North bank of the Brahmaputra; ‘mini Kaziranga’

places.name: Manas NP
places.note: Rhinos reintroduced after being wiped out

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2019: One-horned rhinoceros is naturally found in India & Nepal (not India only).
UPSC CSE Prelims 2013: Kaziranga & Pobitora rhino habitats along Brahmaputra floodplains.

items.title: Asian Elephant
items.subtitle: Elephas maximus
items.oneline: India’s national heritage animal, found in forests from the Himalayan foothills to the Western Ghats.
idmarks: Smaller, rounded ears than the African elephant
Twin-domed head; only some males carry tusks
facts: Karnataka has the largest elephant population among states
Only males (tuskers) carry large tusks in the Asian species
traps: ‘National heritage animal’ is the elephant; ‘national animal’ is the tiger

places.name: Bandipur NP
places.note: Part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve elephant landscape

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2020: Elephant herd led by oldest female; gestation period ~22 months; highest population in Karnataka.
UPSC CSE Prelims 2017: Project Elephant & MIKE (Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants) sites in India.

items.title: Snow Leopard
items.subtitle: Panthera uncia
items.oneline: A grey, spotted cat of the high cold mountains of Ladakh, Himachal, Uttarakhand and Sikkim.
idmarks: Smoky-grey coat with dark open rosettes
Very long, thick tail and broad furry paws
facts: SPAI (2024 report): 718 snow leopards in India
Ladakh holds the largest share
traps: Downlisted from Endangered to Vulnerable in 2017

places.name: Hemis NP
places.note: Densest snow leopard population in India

places.name: Khangchendzonga NP
places.note: India’s first mixed UNESCO World Heritage Site

newsTriggers.what: A ‘Lion’ spotlight event at Sasan Gir was held ahead of India’s first International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Summit in New Delhi.
newsTriggers.why: IBCA is India’s alliance for seven big cats; tiger, lion and snow leopard are among them.

items.title: Red Panda
items.subtitle: Ailurus fulgens
items.oneline: A small reddish tree-dweller of the eastern Himalaya that eats mostly bamboo.
idmarks: Rusty-red fur with white face markings
Bushy tail with alternating light and dark rings
facts: Feeds mostly on bamboo despite being in order Carnivora
Not closely related to the giant panda
traps: Red panda is Endangered; snow leopard is only Vulnerable
programmes: Conservation breeding, Padmaja Naidu Zoo, Darjeeling

items.title: Lion-tailed Macaque
items.subtitle: Macaca silenus
items.oneline: A black monkey with a silver mane, found only in the rainforests of the Western Ghats.
idmarks: Black body with a silver-white mane framing the face
Tail ends in a lion-like tuft
facts: Lives in the upper canopy of tropical evergreen forest
Silver-white mane around a black face
traps: Endemic to the Western Ghats, not found in the North-east

places.name: Silent Valley NP
places.note: Save Silent Valley movement saved its habitat

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2013: Lion-tailed Macaque natural distribution in evergreen rainforests of Western Ghats (Silent Valley, Periyar).

items.title: Nilgiri Tahr
items.subtitle: Nilgiritragus hylocrius
items.oneline: A mountain goat of the southern Western Ghats, and Tamil Nadu’s state animal.
idmarks: Stocky wild goat; adult males dark with a pale ‘saddle’
Short, back-curved horns in both sexes
facts: Mountain ungulate of shola–grassland above about 1,200 m
Eravikulam’s grasslands also host Neelakurinji blooms
traps: Not a goat of the Himalaya: that is the Himalayan tahr

places.name: Mukurthi NP
places.note: Part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2012: Eravikulam National Park holds the largest surviving population of Nilgiri Tahr in Western Ghats montane shola-grasslands.

items.title: Sangai (Brow-antlered Deer)
items.subtitle: Rucervus eldii eldii
items.oneline: Manipur’s ‘dancing deer’, living only on the floating grass mats of Loktak Lake.
idmarks: Brow tine of the antler forms a continuous bow over the eye
Steps delicately on floating phumdis, hence ‘dancing deer’
facts: Phumdis are floating mats of vegetation, soil and organic matter
Loktak Lake is a Ramsar site on the Montreux Record
traps: ‘Dancing deer’ is the Sangai; barasingha is the swamp deer of Kanha

places.name: Keibul Lamjao NP
places.note: World’s only floating national park, on phumdis of Loktak Lake

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2015: Keibul Lamjao National Park (Loktak Lake, Manipur) is the only floating national park on phumdis, home of the dancing deer (Sangai).

items.title: Pygmy Hog
items.subtitle: Porcula salvania
items.oneline: The world’s smallest wild pig, surviving only in a few grasslands of Assam.
idmarks: Tiny: about 25 cm at the shoulder
Dark brown, with a very short tail
facts: Indicator of the health of tall wet grasslands
Has its own host-specific parasite, the pygmy hog-sucking louse
traps: Was Critically Endangered; now Endangered

credit.artist: A. J. T. Johnsingh, WWF-India and NCF

items.title: Western Hoolock Gibbon
items.subtitle: Hoolock hoolock
items.oneline: India’s only ape, swinging through the forests of the North-east.
idmarks: No tail; very long arms
Males black with white brows, females golden-buff
facts: Apes have no tail; monkeys do
Moves by brachiation (arm-swinging)
traps: Gibbon is an ape; lion-tailed macaque is a monkey

places.name: Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary
places.note: India’s only sanctuary named after the gibbon

places.name: Namdapha NP
places.note: Also has the eastern range edge

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2013: The only ape species found in India (Hoolok Gibbon in Assam & North-East evergreen forests).

items.title: Ganges River Dolphin
items.subtitle: Platanista gangetica
items.oneline: India’s national aquatic animal, a nearly blind dolphin of the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.
idmarks: Long, thin beak lined with visible teeth
Tiny eyes and a low hump in place of a dorsal fin
facts: Practically blind; navigates by echolocation
Found in Ganga–Brahmaputra–Meghna and Karnaphuli–Sangu systems
traps: Irrawaddy dolphin of Chilika is a different species

newsTriggers.what: CAMPA approved a recovery plan for the Gangetic dolphin while the second nationwide dolphin survey is running.
newsTriggers.why: Connects dolphins to CAMPA funds, a common Prelims link.

newsTriggers.what: A Wildlife Institute of India study found that falling water flow in the Chambal is pushing dolphins downstream; sightings inside the sanctuary dropped sharply between 2022 and 2026.
newsTriggers.why: River flow decides where river animals can survive.

newsTriggers.what: India’s second nationwide river dolphin survey was launched from Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, led by the Wildlife Institute of India.
newsTriggers.why: The first survey counted about 6,327 dolphins; the new one will update that figure.

newsTriggers.what: India’s first dolphin rescue ambulance was started at the Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun.
newsTriggers.why: A ‘first in India’ fact, often turned into a statement question.

newsTriggers.what: The first-ever estimate of river dolphins in India counted about 6,327.
newsTriggers.why: The baseline figure for the dolphin census.

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2015: Ganges River Dolphin uses echolocation (blind/susu); threatened by barrages, dams & nylon monofilament nets.

items.title: Dugong
items.subtitle: Dugong dugon
items.oneline: A gentle ‘sea cow’ that grazes on seagrass off Tamil Nadu and the Andaman Islands.
idmarks: Fluked, whale-like tail (a manatee has a paddle tail)
Downturned snout for grazing seagrass
facts: ‘Sea cow’ that grazes seagrass
Related to elephants, not to dolphins
traps: Dugong feeds on seagrass, not seaweed
similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2015: Dugong (Sea Cow) is a herbivorous marine mammal found in Gulf of Mannar & Palk Bay; Schedule I of WPA 1972.

items.title: Blackbuck
items.subtitle: Antilope cervicapra
items.oneline: A fast antelope of open grasslands; males have dark coats and spiral horns.
idmarks: Males dark above, white below, with corkscrew spiral horns
Females fawn-coloured and usually hornless
facts: Protected by the Bishnoi community
Moved from Near Threatened to Least Concern in 2017
traps: Least Concern on IUCN, yet Schedule I under WPA: the two lists are independent

places.name: Point Calimere WLS
places.note: Coastal grassland; also a Ramsar site

items.title: Great Indian Bustard
items.subtitle: Ardeotis nigriceps
items.oneline: A large grassland bird of Rajasthan and Gujarat, and one of India’s most threatened birds.
idmarks: Tall, long-necked bird with a black crown on a white head and neck
Males show a black band across the breast
facts: Main threat is collision with overhead power lines
Supreme Court has ordered undergrounding of lines in priority habitat
traps: Heaviest flying bird of India; lives in grassland, not wetland

newsTriggers.what: The first captive-bred Great Indian Bustards, two males, were released into the wild at Sam in Desert National Park, Jaisalmer.
newsTriggers.why: Project GIB has moved from captive breeding to rewilding.

newsTriggers.what: The National Board for Wildlife decided to add the Lesser Florican and the Bengal Florican to the bustard conservation programme.
newsTriggers.why: Floricans are bustards too, so expect them as options in a bustard question.

newsTriggers.what: The first official assessment in seven years found the population stable at about 110–150 birds, surviving in only about 16% of its Thar habitat.
newsTriggers.why: A fresh, official number for a Critically Endangered bird.

newsTriggers.what: A bustard chick hatched in Kutch, Gujarat, for the first time in a decade, using the ‘jumpstart’ method: eggs laid in captivity are placed in wild nests.
newsTriggers.why: Learn the term ‘jumpstart’; it is the kind of new method UPSC likes to test.

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2012 & 2020: Desert National Park primary natural habitat; overhead powerline diverters.

items.title: Forest Owlet
items.subtitle: Athene blewitti
items.oneline: A small owl of central India, once thought extinct; Maharashtra’s Melghat is a key home.
idmarks: Stocky owlet with heavily white-barred wings and tail
Plain, unspotted crown; hunts by day
facts: Rediscovered in 1997 after 113 years without a confirmed record
Active by day, unlike most owls
traps: Downlisted from Critically Endangered to Endangered in 2018

items.title: Jerdon’s Courser
items.subtitle: Rhinoptilus bitorquatus
items.oneline: A rare bird that is active at night, found only in the scrub forests of Andhra Pradesh.
idmarks: Two brown bands across the breast
Bold white eyebrow and a short yellow-based bill
facts: Rediscovered in 1986 after decades without records
Lives in thorny scrub with open patches
traps: Found in the Eastern Ghats, not the Western Ghats

places.name: Sri Lankamalleswara WLS
places.note: Scrub jungle of the Eastern Ghats

items.title: Great Hornbill
items.subtitle: Buceros bicornis
items.oneline: A big forest bird with a huge yellow bill; state bird of Kerala and Arunachal Pradesh.
idmarks: Huge yellow-and-black bill topped by a U-shaped casque
White tail crossed by a broad black band
facts: Female seals herself inside a tree cavity during nesting
Important seed disperser of large-fruited trees
traps: Hornbill Festival is in Nagaland, though the state bird is Blyth’s tragopan

items.title: Gharial
items.subtitle: Gavialis gangeticus
items.oneline: A fish-eating crocodile with a long, thin snout, living mainly in the Chambal river.
idmarks: Very narrow, elongated snout
Adult males carry a bulbous ‘ghara’ on the snout tip
facts: Long, thin snout suited to catching fish
Adult males grow a bulbous ‘ghara’ on the snout tip
traps: Gharial is Critically Endangered; mugger crocodile is Vulnerable

newsTriggers.what: A Wildlife Institute of India study found that falling water flow in the Chambal is pushing dolphins downstream; sightings inside the sanctuary dropped sharply between 2022 and 2026.
newsTriggers.why: River flow decides where river animals can survive.

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2017: National Chambal Sanctuary is the premier wild sanctuary to see Gharials in natural habitat.

items.title: Olive Ridley Turtle
items.subtitle: Lepidochelys olivacea
items.oneline: A sea turtle that comes ashore in thousands to lay eggs on Odisha’s beaches.
idmarks: Smallest sea turtle found in Indian waters
Olive-green, heart-shaped carapace
facts: Arribada: thousands of females nest together
Turtle excluder devices reduce trawl bycatch
traps: Smallest of the sea turtles found in India; leatherback is the largest

places.name: Gahirmatha Marine WLS
places.note: One of the world’s largest rookeries

places.name: Rushikulya rookery
places.note: Mass nesting at the river mouth

similarPYQ: UPSC CSE Prelims 2015: Gahirmatha & Rushikulya mass nesting (Arribada) along the Odisha coast.
